title: Build a comprehensive budget
summary: Track every dollar in and out for at least one full month before optimizing anything.
detailsHtml:
Why this comes first

Personal finance is allocation under constraint. You cannot allocate what you cannot measure. Most "I can't save anything" conclusions dissolve within two weeks of honest tracking — the leak is almost always in subscriptions, restaurants, or convenience purchases that don't survive being itemized.

The mechanics

Capture three numbers: after-tax monthly income, fixed obligations (rent, insurance, loan minimums, recurring subscriptions), and variable spending. The 50/30/20 framework (50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings + above-minimum debt payments) is a reasonable starting allocation, but the real value is in the visibility, not the ratio.

One small refinement: Distinguish your marginal tax rate (the rate on your next dollar earned, used for Roth vs. Traditional decisions) from your effective tax rate (total taxes divided by gross income). Most online calculators get this wrong, and the answers diverge meaningfully.
